newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY O/N RATES CLOSE UNCHANGED AT SOME 18 PCT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY O/N RATES CLOSE UNCHANGED AT SOME 18 PCT.

text.p: Hungarian overnight interest rates closed the last session of the year at levels which dealers called low, amid abundant market liquidity, but little interest in trading.

The overnight rates, which usually move around the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) one-week reverse repo rate -- currently 21.75 percent -- ended Tuesday's lacklustre trading at around 18 percent, unchanged from Monday.
"At this (low) level there was neither buying nor selling interest," said Marton Kerekes of Europai Kereskedelmi Bank, adding that funds flowed into one-week reverse repo deals.
Dealers said that they expected the market to remain liquid in the first part of January.

They added that the most remarkable change of the interbank forint market this year was that the NBH's management of its repo rates and the increasing expertise of the players shaved off most of the extremities of 1995, when the overnight rates often rose to extremely high or fell to very low levels.
